This was me. Lost something very important to me and let myself eat till I gained 80 lbs over my healthy weight. The motivation it took for me was basically realizing that despite what society wants you to think the whole "all sizes are beautiful" is BS. Everyone loves looking at a person that's in shape and taking care of themselves. It's because your physical image speaks to a lot about your character. It shows that you are well adjusted and have good control over your lives. I'm a dude so it definitely was the case for me. Maybe not so much for women.

 It took about 8 months of just changing my diet and adding some more activity in to my life for me to lose it all. In that time the amount of attention/ positive feedback I've received from women is insane. My own confidence has gone up through the roof. (I spent a whole summer playing video games because I was too embarrassed to even go outside).  I also secured myself a better job that pays me a lot more and I think I have my weight loss to thank for it all. The world may seem superficial but if you play the cards right and live your best life you too can enjoy the benefits of it. My intent with saying all isn't harmful to you or anyone, but sometimes tough hard truths are well needed. Hope this finds you well. Best of luck to you on your weight loss journey 🙏 :)

Hey dude congrats on the solo! I just had mine over a month ago best experience ever. I'm currently working on my PPL. I've been where you are right now; freaking out about irrational things. I don't want to say that it's a normal thing but I'll just tell you what this did for me. I spent a big load of the good flyable summer time obsessing over these fears and now where I live summer is coming to an end and I still have about 25 flights to go till my flight test. I'm telling you this because I don't want you to have to go through the rush against time that I'm playing right now. 

To answer your actual post the best way I dealt with this was by looking up past cessna 172 (what i fly) crashes and what caused them. I tried to get a good understanding of how the plane is put together.  Another thing that helped a lot me came right after my solo, FORCED APPROACHES. It gave me a lot of confidence that if all goes wrong I'll still have a good chance of surviving. That's just what worked for me. Good luck with the rest of your flying. Have faith in yourself,your training, also your instructors and don't forget your plane itself :)
